items.description: Travis Kelce has publicly backed Patrick Mahomes’ Kansas City Current ahead of the 2026 NWSL Championship final. items.title: Ohio landlord mistakenly removes tenant's art; court upholds her $6,000 award
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Grace Davis was awarded $6,000 by an Ohio court after her landlord mistakenly discarded her personal belongings. Despite lacking receipts or photographs, she provided a detailed list with estimated values. The landlord's management company challenged the award, arguing that sufficient proof was missing. The appeals court upheld the ruling, stating that the unique nature of the items justified Davis's valuation.

items.title: Nasa picked 10 of 8,000 astronaut applicants; next class deadline December 3
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.

items.title: LA's iconic diner reopens as nonprofit serving meals to help homeless people
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.

items.title: Swiss Alps ice retreat reveals 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring on mountain pass
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.
